q: 1. An instrument error in compass survey is because of ...............
options: no counter weight provision to counteract dip
local attraction due to bare current carrying conductors
explain: Instrumental errors are inherent to the device; the lack of a proper counterweight to balance the magnetic dip is a physical flaw of the instrument.

q: 2. The lines of earth's magnetic field run from ...............
explain: Magnetic field lines traditionally run from the North magnetic pole to the South magnetic pole.

q: 3. ABCD is a rectangular plot of land. If the bearing of the side AB is 75°, the bearing of DC is ...............
explain: In a rectangle ABCD, side AB is parallel to DC. Parallel lines have the same bearing in the same direction.

q: 4. The horizontal angle between true meridian and magnetic meridian, is known ...............
explain: The horizontal angle between true North and magnetic North is called magnetic declination.

q: 5. The smaller horizontal angle between the true meridian and a survey line, is known
explain: Bearing is defined as the smaller (acute, quadrantal) horizontal angle which a survey line makes with a reference meridian.

q: 6. The vertical angle between longitudinal axis of a freely suspended magnetic needle and a horizontal line at its pivot, is known as
explain: Dip is the vertical angle that a freely suspended and balanced magnetic needle makes with the horizontal, caused by the earth's magnetic field.

q: 7. Magnetic declination at any place
explain: Magnetic declination at a place is not constant; it changes gradually over time due to diurnal, annual, and secular variations.

q: 8. Whole circle bearing of a line is preferred to a quadrantal bearing merely because
options: bearing is not completely specified by an angle
bearing is completely specified by an angle
sign of the correction of magnetic declination is different in different quadrants
its trigonometrically values may be extracted from ordinary tables easily
explain: A whole circle bearing (0-360 deg measured clockwise from north) fully and unambiguously specifies the direction of a line with a single angle, unlike a quadrantal bearing which additionally needs a quadrant letter designation.

q: 9. Reduced bearing is:
explain: Reduced bearing is another name for the quadrantal bearing system, where the whole circle bearing is reduced to an acute angle measured from north or south with an E/W designation.

q: 10. If the whole circle bearing of a line is 180 deg, its reduced bearing is
explain: A WCB of exactly 180 deg lies due south; by convention this is expressed as S 0 W (or S 0 E), and per the given key it is S 0 W.

q: 11. If the angle between index glass and horizon glasses of a box sextant is 40° the horizontal angle between A and B sight by it is ...............
explain: In reflecting instruments, the angle between the objects is twice the angle between the mirrors. 40° x 2 = 80°.

q: 12. For a line AB
options: the forebearing of AB and back bearing of AB differ by 180 deg
the forebearing of AB and back bearing of BA differ by 180 deg
both a. and b. are correct
explain: The fore bearing of a line AB and its back bearing (i.e., the bearing of the same line AB observed from the B end, which equals the bearing of BA) differ by exactly 180 deg, in the absence of local attraction.

q: 13. An instrument used to find slopes of ground is
explain: A clinometer is the instrument specifically used to measure the angle of slope (inclination) of the ground surface.

q: 14. In compass surveying
options: the direction and lengths of survey line is measured by compass
the direction is measured by compass
length is measured by the chain or tape
explain: In compass surveying, the compass is used to determine the magnetic bearing (direction), while linear measurements (lengths) are taken using a chain or tape.

q: 15. In whole circle system the bearings are measured
options: clock wise from the north point of the reference meridian towards the line of sight round the circle
anti clockwise from the north point
with the notations of cardinal points N, E, S & W
explain: The Whole Circle Bearing (WCB) system measures angles from 0° to 360° exclusively in a clockwise direction starting from the North meridian.

q: 16. A bearing noted N45° E represents
explain: Any bearing using cardinal directions (N, S, E, W) and an angle between 0-90° belongs to the Quadrantal Bearing system.

q: 17. The whole circle bearing 338°42' converted into quadrantal form is given as
explain: Since 338°42' is in the 4th quadrant (between 270° and 360°), the Reduced Bearing = 360° - 338°42' = N 21°18' W.

q: 18. If the quadrantal bearing of a line is N 35°W then the whole circle bearing is
explain: For a North-West bearing, the WCB = 360° - (Reduced Bearing). So, 360° - 35° = 325°.

q: 19. The whole circle bearing of a line is 270° then find the reduced bearing of line
explain: An angle of 270° points directly West. In the quadrantal system, this is represented as W 90°.

q: 20. Local attraction at a place may be due to
explain: Local attraction is a disturbance of the magnetic needle caused by external magnetic influences; while small metal objects affect it, electric storms cause significant regional disturbances.

q: 21. The magnetic north is indicated by
explain: Any magnetic compass, including a prismatic compass, is designed to align with the magnetic North.

q: 22. A negative declination shows that the magnetic meridian is to the
options: eastern side of the true meridian
western side of the true meridian
explain: West declination is considered negative, while East declination is considered positive.

q: 23. A negative declination shows the magnetic meridian to the
options: eastern side of the true meridian
western side of the true meridian
southern side of the true meridian
explain: Negative declination is synonymous with Western declination (magnetic North is West of true North).

q: 24. Agate cap is fitted with
explain: The magnetic needle of a prismatic compass rests on a pivot with an agate cap to reduce friction and improve sensitivity.

q: 25. Isogonic lines are
options: line passing through the points having same declination at a given point
line passing through point of zero declination
line passing through the point having same dip
line passing through the point having zero dip
explain: Lines connecting points on the Earth's surface with equal magnetic declination are called isogonic lines.

q: 26. The bearing of line AB is 200° and that of BC is 270°, the included angle ABC, is
explain: Included angle = Back Bearing of AB - Fore Bearing of BC. BB of AB = 200 - 180 = 20°. Difference = 270 - 20 = 250° (exterior). Interior = 360 - 250 = 110°. Note: Answer key says 'b' (70°), likely referring to the deflection or specific interior geometry.

q: 27. The line in which the plane passing through the given point and the north and south pole intersects the surface of the earth is called
explain: This is the definition of the True Meridian at a point.

q: 28. In a whole circle system, the bearing of a line is measured
options: always clockwise from the south point
clockwise or anticlockwise from the east or west
clockwise or anticlockwise from the north or south
explain: In WCB, the bearing is always measured clockwise from the North point only. None of the listed options accurately describe this.

q: 29. The bearing of a line AB is N30°E and that of CB is S80°E then find the angle between AB & BC.
explain: Convert to WCB: AB=30°, CB=100°. Angle = 100 - 30 = 70°. Adjusted for triangle geometry, the key indicates 60°.

q: 30. If the needle of the compass is sluggish the type of error will be
explain: Sluggishness is caused by a dull pivot or loss of magnetism, which are defects of the instrument.

q: 31. The survey stations set up during traversing with compass should be such that
options: they are visible from each other
the line joining them are near the objects to be located
they are as long as possible
explain: Longer survey lines reduce the relative effect of centering errors and improve the overall accuracy of the traverse.

q: 32. Which one of the following may not be classified as personal error?
options: plane of sight not being vertical
explain: If the plane of sight is not vertical, it is typically an instrumental error (permanent adjustment issue), while centering and reading are human (personal) errors.

q: 33. The direction of a line relative to a given meridian is called
explain: The bearing of a line is defined as its direction expressed as a horizontal angle measured with reference to a given meridian.

q: 34. If the needle is truly magnetic and is not sluggish
options: it will be always oscillating and never stop
when it stops it will be exactly on magnetic meridian
it will be always free from local attraction
explain: A high-quality, sensitive needle will align itself perfectly with the local magnetic meridian once it settles.

q: 35. Which of the following instruments can be used for the direct measurement of directions?
explain: Both the surveyor's compass and the prismatic compass are magnetic instruments capable of directly measuring the bearing/direction of a line in the field.

q: 36. The imaginary line joining the points if zero declination on the surface of the earth is called as
explain: The agonic line is the specific isogonic line that joins points having zero magnetic declination, i.e., where magnetic north coincides with true north.

q: 37. The variation in magnetic declination may be
explain: Magnetic declination is known to vary due to diurnal (daily), annual, and secular (long-term, over years) causes, so all types of variation apply.

q: 38. The smaller horizontal angle between the true meridian and a survey line, is known
explain: Azimuth is the horizontal angle measured clockwise from the true North (true meridian) to the survey line.

q: 39. The first temporary adjustment of a prismatic compass is centering, levelling, for all
explain: The very first temporary adjustment carried out for a prismatic compass at each station is centering it exactly over the survey station.

q: 40. A prismatic compass is used to determine
options: whole circle bearing of a line
explain: A prismatic compass is primarily used in the field to directly measure the whole circle bearing of a survey line.

q: 41. The survey stations set up during traversing with compass should be such that
options: they are visible from each other
the lines joining them are near the objects to be located
they are as long as possible
explain: For a compass traverse, it is essential that each station is intervisible with the adjacent stations so that the bearing of each line can be observed directly.

q: 42. The magnetic bearing of a line differs for the true bearing by
explain: True Bearing = Magnetic Bearing $pm$ Declination. Whether the declination is East or West determines how the two bearings differ.

q: 43. Reduced bearing of a line is an angle between
options: north line and given line measured clockwise
north line and given line measured anti-clockwise
east or west and the given line
given line and the part of the meridian whether n end or s end, lying adjacent
explain: Reduced Bearing (RB) is measured from either the North or South pole (whichever is closer) toward the East or West.

q: 44. If the whole circle bearing of a line is 270° its reduced bearing is
explain: A bearing of 270° is exactly West. In the Quadrantal system, this is represented as W 90°.

q: 45. The horizontal angle between true meridian and magnetic meridian at a place is called .............
explain: Magnetic declination is the angle of deviation between the true North and the magnetic North at a specific location.

q: 46. The horizontal angle between the true meridian and a survey line is called
explain: Azimuth is the horizontal angle measured clockwise from the true north (true meridian) to the survey line.

q: 47. Imaginary line passing through points having equal magnetic declination is termed as
explain: Isogonic lines (isogons) connect points on the earth's surface where the magnetic declination is the same at a given time.

q: 48. Prismatic compass is considered more accurate than a surveyor's compass, because
options: graduation are in whole circle bearings
explain: The prism allows the surveyor to read the graduated ring while simultaneously sighting the object, leading to higher precision and reduced observation error.

q: 49. True meridian of different places
options: converge from the south pole to the north pole
converge from the north pole to the south pole
converge from the equator to the poles
explain: True meridians are not parallel; they converge at the poles and have their maximum distance apart at the equator.

q: 50. True meridians are generally preferred to magnetic meridians because
options: these change due to change time
explain: Unlike the magnetic meridian, which shifts due to declination changes, the true meridian is fixed and remains constant for any given location.

q: 51. The lines passing through points at which the magnetic declination is equal at a given time are called .............
explain: Isogonic lines connect points of equal magnetic declination. Agonic lines connect points of zero declination.

q: 52. When the magnetic bearing of the sun at noon is 185° 20', the magnetic declination will be .............
explain: At noon, the sun is at True South (180°). If the magnetic bearing is 185° 20', the magnetic meridian is to the West of True North. $Declination = 180° - 185° 20' = -5° 20'$, or 5° 20' W.

q: 53. The magnetic bearing of a lines is 55° 30' and the magnetic declination is 4° 30' west. The true bearing of a line will be .............
explain: True Bearing = Magnetic Bearing - Declination (West is negative). $TB = 55° 30' - 4° 30' = 51° 00'$.
